text:
ravi: Heads-up — want to align on a lightweight gating heuristic for onboarding new models. TL;DR proposal: 3-min smoke + tiny benchmark (5 samples) measuring latency, p50/p95, cost estimate, and a golden-output parity check. Thoughts?

ciara: +1 to a fast gate. Main worry: kv-cache/runtime ABI mismatches and tokenization differences can pass the smoke but break at scale. Suggest adding a KV warmup and a small tokenization diff check (compare token counts & first/last token ids).

mel: Agree w/ ciara. Also we need a concrete adapter metadata contract so adapters declare capabilities up-front. Minimal required fields: `vocab_hash`, `max_ctx`, `dtype`, `kv_compatible`, `quantized_profile`. If missing -> fail fast.

jord: Can we keep this ingest synchronous? Ideally adapter returns a `handshake.json` during register that the intake pipeline validates. That avoids a separate post-ingest probe step. Example handshake snippet:```
model_handshake:
  vocab_hash: "sha256:..."
  max_ctx: 8192
  dtype: "fp16"
  kv_compatible: true
  quantized_profile: "q4_0"
```

ravi: Nice. Operationally I want two tiers of checks: "smoke" (fast, gating for immediate ingest) and "bench-horizon" (slower, tuned sampling that runs asynchronously and can mark model as "probation"). Smoke must finish < 5 min; bench-horizon can be up to 2 hours.

ciara: For the smoke gate: 1) tokenization diff check, 2) KV warmup (run 8 step prefix to ensure cache shape), 3) 5 sample latency/cost run. If any of these hits a hard failure -> reject.

mel: Bench-horizon should capture distributional inputs: short, medium, long tokens, and a few adversarial prompts we store in the golden set. Also track quality regression via a lightweight similarity metric (BERTscore-ish) against golden outputs. Not perfect but catches gross regressions.

jord: We need to define signal thresholds. Proposal: latency p95 < 2x reference model for same hw, tokenization parity >= 95%, kv-compat boolean, quality similarity > 0.8. Flags: warn if near thresholds; fail if crossed.

bench-bot: AUTO: scheduled bench-horizon run queued for model 'x-demo' (id: m-123). ETA ~ 90m. Results will be posted to #eng-ml/bench-results.

ravi: Question about sampling: do we do deterministic sampling from our golden corpus or random draws? Deterministic helps reproducibility; random helps surface edgecases. Maybe seed-based hybrid: deterministic core + seeded fuzz set.

ciara: +1 on hybrid. Also add a run that performs a prefix-aligned KV test: feed same prefix across batch sizes to detect KV shape bugs. This is a cheap check but catches a lot.

mel: On the adapter contract side, we should version the handshake schema (handshake_v1) and enforce a compatibility table. If we bump the schema we'll require adapters to opt-in. Keeps back-compat manageable.

jord: UX: intake API returns a single object with `status:{smoke:pass/warn/fail, bench_horizon:pending/complete}` and `actions` list with suggested next steps (e.g., "increase ctx config", "submit adapter patch"). Keeps operators from guessing.

ravi: OK next steps: 1) ciara to draft smoke checklist runnable as one `ingest-smoke` CLI (due EOD Wed), 2) mel to write handshake_v1 schema PR and example fixtures (due Thu), 3) jord to draft intake response shape + UX (due Fri). I'll follow up with a short RFC update summarizing thresholds.

ciara: noted. will add KV warmup commands & tokenization diff to the CLI.

mel: will sketch handshake_v1 in a repo fiddle and link in RFC.

jord: I'll mock the intake API response and add examples for common failure messages.

ravi: Thanks all. If bench-bot posts failures for any model, let's triage in a separate thread per model. :thumbsup:

bench-bot: NOTE: when bench-horizon completes it will post a compact JSON blob with metrics and `decision` (pass/warn/fail) to #eng-ml/bench-results.
